mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by at least 0.50 percentage points over three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a high-inflation regime where real rates remain negative.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 3% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls by more than 3% year-over-year
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when accompanied by simultaneous large fiscal stimulus.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by more than 1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a period of strong export demand.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation above 2% for two consecutive months signals a dual tightening in monetary and real terms, which increases borrowing costs and reduces real purchasing power, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 2% and CPIAUCSL > 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when fiscal stimulus offsets monetary tightening.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1 million units for four consecutive months signals a housing market downturn, which reduces construction-related economic activity and drags on broader GDP growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong mortgage rate declines.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over a two-month period indicates a paradoxical labor market signal, often preceding a sharp correction, and predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE increases over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of extreme market volatility unrelated to labor data.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annualized decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below -2% for three consecutive months signals a consumer deleveraging phase, which reduces discretionary spending and corporate revenue, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < -2% annualized for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong credit expansion.
